description: The Electric Grid Test Case Repository at Texas A&M University publishes synthetic power system test cases that are statistically and functionally similar to real grids but contain no Critical Energy Infrastructure Information. It includes the ACTIVSg series from 200 to 82,000 buses on footprints of US regions, developed partly under the US DOE ARPA-E GridData programme, the EPIGRIDS grids from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Texas synthetic cases with 6,717 buses including versions with distribution and with natural gas pipelines, the Texas2k Series24 and Series25 cases with 2025-level wind, solar and batteries, a 2026 Memphis case, an Oahu island case, ARPA-E PERFORM and GO Competition cases and classic literature cases such as the IEEE 14 to 300-bus systems. Coverage is synthetic footprints of US regions and states, plus literature cases. Cases come in PowerWorld, MATPOWER, PSS/E and PSLF formats, some with OpenDSS distribution data, and flags show which include transient stability, geomagnetic disturbance, optimal power flow and synthetic PMU data; every case has a feasible AC power flow solution. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-1.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: the grids are fictitious, so they suit method testing, not analysis of real assets. Simulation uses are power flow, optimisation, cascading failure, geomagnetic hazard and gas-electric interdependency studies. Related records: the cases are distributed in the format of model-matpower.
